newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Saab Automobile sees new model sales at 10,000 '97.
newsitem.headline: Saab Automobile sees new model sales at 10,000 '97.

text.p: Swedish-U.S. car maker Saab Automobile said on Friday it expected to sell more than 100,000 cars this year with sales of its new 9-5 model reaching around 10,000.
Saab Automobile is a 50-50 joint venture held by Swedish investment company Investor and U.S. automotive group General Motors (GM).
"We expect sales of Saab cars to exceed 100,000 cars in 1997," Saab Automobile spokesman Olle Axelsson told Reuters. "We expect 10 percent of the sold cars to be of the 9-5 model."

Saab is targetting total sales of 150,000 cars in 2000, of which the 9-5 model is expected to account for almost half, the smaller 900 series for about the same and the larger 9000 series for around 10,000, Axelsson said.
